teaching_suggestions: Acknowledge the effective use of a friendly tone and conversational style, which fosters a welcoming environment. To enhance engagement, consider incorporating more interactive elements during announcements, such as asking students to respond to specific questions or share their thoughts in the chat, especially when discussing important changes like the class schedule.

While the pacing is steady, it may benefit from being more concise, particularly when delivering announcements. For example, when explaining the schedule changes, try to summarize key points in a few sentences and then invite questions. This can help maintain student attention and reduce cognitive overload, aligning with the goal of keeping students engaged.

To improve interaction, explicitly invite students to share their thoughts or experiences related to the announcements. For instance, after discussing the upcoming assignments, ask students how they feel about the workload or if they have any strategies they would like to share. This can create a more collaborative atmosphere and encourage participation.

Reflect on the moments when students seemed less engaged, such as during lengthy explanations about the rubric. Consider breaking down complex information into smaller, digestible parts and using visual aids or examples to illustrate your points. This approach can help clarify expectations and maintain student interest.

Encourage self-reflection by setting aside a few minutes after each class to evaluate which parts of the lesson engaged students the most and which did not. Use this reflection to adjust future lessons, focusing on maintaining high engagement levels by incorporating more interactive and concise elements.
